articles.title: Troy Aikman, Joe Buck reportedly got into argument in 'Monday Night Football' booth over contract extension tensions at ESPN
articles.summary: Joe Buck has signed a $100 million extension with ESPN, but Troy Aikman still has not.
articles.body:
Tensions are apparently running high inside the "Monday Night Football" booth.

Longtime broadcaster Joe Buck and Hall of Fame quarterback Troy Aikman got into an argument inside the announcer booth at SoFi Stadium ahead of Monday night's game between the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills, according to Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel .

Buck and Aikman's relationship has reportedly been strained ever since Buck reportedly reached a new contract with ESPN last month that is reportedly worth more than $100 million over the next six seasons. The new deal will ensure that Buck will call the Super Bowl both this year and again when ESPN/ABC gets the rights to it in 2031.

Aikman, however, has not received a formal offer on a new deal.

So on Monday night, according to Glasspiegel, Buck "broke the ice" on the unspoken tension between the two. That led to an argument, which eventually de-escalated before the game started. The game carried on normally, and Buck and Aikman called the game without issue.

Aikman spent 12 seasons playing with the Cowboys, and he led the franchise to three Super Bowl titles before he retired after the 2000 campaign. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2006.

Aikman quickly transitioned into broadcasting after his playing career ended, and he joined Buck at Fox in 2002. The pair are the longest-tenured broadcast team in NFL history, and have undoubtedly become among the most recognizable voices in the sport. They left Fox for ESPN in 2022. Aikman reached his contract with ESPN first, and Buck followed weeks later.

It's not known what would happen to Aikman should he split with ESPN after the Super Bowl. While there are several potential landing spots for him at other networks, an NFL world without the Aikman-Buck pairing is one that the sport hasn't seen in decades.

articles.title: Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Status for Texans-Jaguars Revealed, WR's Fantasy Outlook After Cardinals Trade
articles.summary: Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is expected to make his Houston Texans debut Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Wednesday.
articles.body:
Wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. is expected to make his Houston Texans debut Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London, head coach DeMeco Ryans told reporters Wednesday.

The Texans sent a package including a 2027 second-round pick to the Arizona Cardinals in order to acquire Harrison from the Cardinals on Monday.

Ryans said he expects Harrison to play Sunday but see somewhat limited usage during the Week 6 matchup.

"When you get a player come in late, like Marvin has, it's just, again, what is he able to pick up on?" Ryans said Wednesday. "We'll go through the entire playbook. We'll have set plays, and we'll make sure it's as easy as possible for him to get lined up so he can play fast.

"Don't expect him to come out and play all 60 snaps in a game, but we'll make sure he gets what he needs, and make sure he's confident in what we're asking him to do."

Harrison has experience playing with Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud from their overlapping time at Ohio State.

That could potentially help Harrison eventually make his case for an increase over his workload in Arizona, where Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett targeted him just 13 times for five catches in four games this season.

Harrison was listed as inactive for the Cardinals' Week 5 matchup before he was traded Monday. He joined Stroud and the Texans for his first team practice Wednesday.

Ryans expressed hope Harrison would be able to quickly adjust to the Texans system after beginning work on the playbook the night he arrived in Houston.

"Getting a player caught up, it isn't hard when the player is attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down... I'm excited to see how his week continues to progress, and see how much he can handle," Ryans said.

Stroud has been leaning this season on Nico Collins, who despite missing two games leads the Texans with 249 receiving yards.

Ryans said he is "excited" to see Harrison and Collins play together in part because he feels both receivers for contested catches.

Harrison is listed as backup to Collins on the Texans' unofficial depth chart. Should Harrison establish himself as a WR2, he could potentially take snaps away from Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte, while Jaylin Noel could continue serving as the Texans' slot receiver going forward.

It could take some time for Harrison to establish himself as the Texans' second option behind Collins.

Even in the short term, however, the limited usage Harrison saw as a Cardinal and the Texans' pass-first offense could mean the third-year wide receiver will see a boost in usage as soon as Sunday's game in London.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Praises Marvin Harrison Jr., Says 'Special' WR Will Be 'Great' for Texans After Trade
articles.summary: Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has been impressed with Marvin Harrison Jr. after the team recently acquired the wide receiver in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud has been impressed with Marvin Harrison Jr. after the team recently acquired the wide receiver in a trade with the Arizona Cardinals.

"I've always thought he was special," Stroud said Wednesday, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. "His work ethic, it's the same thing now"

He also detailed how they work together on the field.

"Runs great routes, very quarterback friendly receiver," Stroud explained, per Wilson . "I'm a pocket quarterback who likes to throw it to him on time. That's when he's at his best."

Stroud and Harrison are already familiar with playing alongside each other, previously spending time together at Ohio State from 2021-22.

Stroud also envisioned Harrison as a strong fit in a receiving corps that includes Nico Collins, Kayshon Boutte, Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel.

"He'll fit in fine," Stroud said regarding Harrison, per Wilson . "He'll be great for us."

Houston added Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round draft pick from Arizona in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a seventh-round pick on Sunday.

Expectations were high for Harrison after the Cardinals selected him with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft.

While he started off slow as a rookie, he still finished his inaugural season with 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns.

Harrison took a step back the following year, hauling in 41 receptions for 608 yards and four scores. It's worth noting that he missed five games due to injuries .

Still, Harrison wasn't able to establish himself as a threat in Arizona's passing attack to begin this season. In four appearances, he caught just five passes for 85 yards and one touchdown.

The 24-year-old will look to get his career back on track following the change of scenery.

Houston has dealt with several injuries to its wide receivers in 2026, as Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL in training camp while Tank Dell has yet to make his season debut as he recovers from a knee injury .

The Texans own a mere 1-4 record, although they're looking to turn their season around and clinch a fourth consecutive playoff berth. Houston started 0-3 in 2025, but still finished at 12-5 and advanced to the postseason.

Stroud has been efficient to open his 2026 campaign despite Houston's overall struggles, completing 64.3 percent of his throws for 1,402 yards and six touchdowns without getting picked off.

articles.title: Carolina Panthers lineman Taylor Moton overcame bloody, life-threatening episode and now he's back at practice
articles.summary: Taylor Moton describes coughing up blood and the terrifying discovery of multiple clots in his right lung that put his life at serious risk.
articles.body: This is a comeback story of the highest order because Taylor Moton's life was at risk, blood was splattered all over his chest, and doctors frantically rushed to keep him from dying from a life-threatening emergency. Moton is a Carolina Panthers offensive lineman. Except, he hasn't been an offensive lineman since the offseason because he was exclusively a patient trying to overcome the condition that caused, as he put it, "a multitude of clots in my right lung." DEION SANDERS DECLARES HE'S CANCER-FREE, ADDRESSES INCONTINENCE AHEAD OF COLORADO FOOTBALL SEASON People die from runaway blood clots. I had a friend die from blood clots in 2022. Miami Dolphins senior vice president Jason Jenkins died from a bilateral pulmonary thromboembolism due to phlebothrombosis. He was in his office at the team's training facility when it happened. Jenkins had complained of the pain clots in his legs caused him for months before that. He talked about how he had to be careful when he flew because that could impact his condition. So when Moton was placed on the non-football injury list in July it caught my attention because there had been reports about it being tied to clots since June. And that was extremely worrisome. But this column isn't all about sadness and concern. Or death. HOUSTON TEXANS STAR PRACTICES IN PADS FOR FIRST TIME IN NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER 2024 CAREER-THREATENING INJURY That's because Moton is back on the Panthers practice field this week. And he was in the locker room on Tuesday talking about his victory over a life-threatening condition. "I was just hanging out about to take a nap, lay down, and all of sudden it started to feel like my chest was really congested," Moton told a group of reporters gathered at his locker. "I thought it was just normal chest congestion. But I started to taste blood in my mouth and then I knew something was up." One can only imagine what a world-class athlete who hadn't yet reached his 32nd birthday thinks when confronted with a serious medical emergency. These guys train to feel invincible. But Moton immediately realized he wasn't invincible. He was in deep trouble. "I started coughing up blood -- and it was like a lot of it," Moton said. "And I could start feeling it leaking through my chest even -- something like really different. So, after 15-or-something minutes, I was like 'Yeah, I've got to go to the hospital.' "Went to the hospital, they were doing CT scans, ultrasounds, trying to find what was going on. And that's when they found a multitude of clots in my right lung." Stunning. "They put me on blood thinners, and other than that I was just working," he said. "I just couldn't have contact on the blood thinners because having contact on blood thinners can lead to like a brain bleed." Moton has been trying to stay in shape but it clearly isn't football shape. So he has 21 days to try to reach that kind of physical conditioning before a decision on his season's availability has to be made. The Panthers, dealing with injuries on their offensive line, need him as soon as possible. The man they're getting back has a different outlook than the one who last played a game in the 2025 season. "When you see the blood, you start thinking the worst," Moton said. "But thank God I'm still on this side of Earth, right? Like past football, man, it makes you count your blessings to be here. articles.title: Alaric Jackson's Suspension for Punching Bradley Chubb Reduced By NFL After Rams' Loss to Bills
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams are reportedly likely to be without left tackle Alaric Jackson for the next two games.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams will be without left tackle Alaric Jackson for just Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals after his two-game suspension was reduced to one game upon appeal.

He's eligible to return on October 25 against the Las Vegas Raiders.

The NFL initially announced Tuesday that Jackson had been suspended for two games after he punched Buffalo Bills pass-rusher Bradley Chubb following Monday night's game.

With players gathering on the field after Buffalo's 37-34 victory, there was an altercation that resulted in Jackson throwing a punch and Chubb's teammates restraining him.

The situation even appeared to catch Josh Allen's attention during a postgame interview:

ESPN's Sarah Barshop noted Jackson was exchanging jerseys with Bills defensive lineman Deone Walker when Chubb appeared to say something. The offensive lineman responded by approaching Chubb and punching him.

"Somebody swung, but hey, that's not on me to tell who," Chubb told reporters in the aftermath. "There's cameras out there. I just know, you know what I'm saying, I'm just ready for next week."

He also said, "It was an emotional game. Tempers got flared. But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."

It was a back-and-forth game, as there were a combined five touchdowns in the fourth quarter alone with Allen and Matthew Stafford exchanging impressive plays and directing drives. It seemed like Buffalo would win when James Cook's touchdown and the ensuing extra point put it up seven with 1:39 remaining, but the Rams responded with a 63-yard touchdown drive of their own to force overtime.

Overtime featured Cook losing a fumble, the Rams' game-winning field-goal attempt being blocked and Tyler Bass connecting on his field goal on the ensuing possession to win it.

For his part, Chubb finished with two tackles when facing Jackson and the rest of the Rams offensive line. Neither defense likely felt great about their efforts on Monday, although the dominant offenses deserve plenty of credit.

With Jackson suspended for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, look for David Quessenberry to potentially fill in for the starter until he returns.

articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. left Sunday's game with a rib injury and was replaced by Tua Tagovailoa in overtime, but he's set to start against Chicago.
articles.body: The quarterback situation in Atlanta has been one of the NFL’s most closely watched storylines. After an offseason marked by injuries and a two-week stint with Cooper Rush under center, Atlanta appeared to find some stability when Michael Penix Jr. returned to the starting lineup. Late in Sunday’s hard-fought game against the Baltimore Ravens, Penix sustained a rib injury on a sack. He briefly returned before the end of regulation but could not continue in overtime, forcing Tua Tagovailoa to take over. Tagovailoa threw the game-ending interception, leaving Penix’s status for a pivotal Week 6 meeting with the Chicago Bears uncertain. After Penix underwent an MRI earlier this week, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday that the quarterback is on track to start Sunday’s game, barring any setbacks. Penix was back at practice Wednesday, although he was listed as a limited participant. BACKUP QUARTERBACK TYLER HUNTLEY LEADS BALTIMORE RAVENS TO IMPROBABLE OT WIN OVER ATLANTA FALCONS Stefanski stopped short of offering details about what he knew about the extent of Penix's rib injury, instead telling reporters that the left-handed thrower is "feeling better." On Monday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter told "The Pat McAfee Show" that Penix’s rib injury "didn’t look like it’s a long-term injury" at the time. Penix’s practice workload this week will depend on how he feels, Stefanski said. "I want to see how he's feeling," Stefanski said. "With any injury like this, you want to make sure as they move around and how they're feeling -- it could be all, some, none. We shall see." ESPN reported later on Wednesday that Penix "took all the first-team reps in practice." "I felt good today at practice," Penix told reporters when asked the status of his ribs. "… I just gotta stay on top of my rehab and just make sure I'm doing all the right things." He added: "I feel good to go this week, so that's the plan." Penix’s injury history, dating back to his college days, is well documented. He suffered his latest ACL injury last November and underwent surgery. articles.title: 4 Arrested in the Shooting of San Francisco 49ers Player Keion White at a Super Bowl Party
articles.summary: SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting of San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Keion White at a nightclub in February, officials said Wednesday.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO (AP) — Four men have been arrested in connection with the shooting of San Francisco 49ers defensive lineman Keion White at a nightclub in February, officials said Wednesday.

The shooting occurred just after 4 a.m. on Feb. 9 at the crowded Mission District nightclub Dahlia, where White was hosting a private Super Bowl party.

White was shot in the ankle and taken to a local hospital for surgery, his team said at the time.

San Francisco Police Chief Derrick Lew said authorities arrested four men over the past week with the help of law enforcement agencies in Atlanta; Stockton, California; Irvine, California and Los Angeles.

The night of the shooting, multiple suspects with firearms "confronted" White, Lew said. Investigators used video footage and witness accounts to identify the men they say are the perpetrators.

On Oct. 7, local law enforcement arrested 35-year-old Curtis Green in Irvine, and two days later authorities arrested 36-year-old Gregory Walker of Mountain House, California, for their alleged involvement in the shooting.

The men were booked into San Francisco County Jail on Monday and scheduled to appear in court Wednesday afternoon. District Attorney Brooke Jenkins said prosecutors would seek no bail for Walker due to the public safety risk they said he poses. He will be charged with assault with a semiautomatic firearm — which prosecutors say he fired — as well as other charges for having a gun as a felon.

Green faces misdemeanor charges of brandishing a firearm and carrying a concealed and loaded gun in public, Jenkins said.

A message was left Wednesday with the San Francisco public defender's office to determine if its attorneys were representing the two men.

Two other men arrested in other jurisdictions are not yet in local custody and will be charged once they are brought to San Francisco, Jenkins said.

One of the other men expected to face charges in San Francisco was arrested Oct. 7 in Atlanta. The 38-year-old was arrested on a no-bail warrant. Authorities say police seized an illegal firearm during the arrest, along with thousands of grams of MDMA, methamphetamine, cocaine and fentanyl at the man's home.

That same day, law enforcement arrested a 36-year-old man in Stockton, California, in connection with White's shooting, and recovered a loaded firearm, over 100 oxycodone pills and $7,000 in cash.

Surtain was officially ruled out Wednesday with an ankle injury after missing practice throughout the week. The timing could hardly be worse for Denver. The Broncos are preparing to face Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who currently leads the NFL in receiving yards with 583 through five games.

Pat Surtain's absence is a massive problem

Jan 4, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II (2) reacts with safety Devon Key (26) after a play in the fourth quarter against the Los Angeles Chargers at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images

Surtain isn't just another starting cornerback. The former NFL Defensive Player of the Year is the centerpiece of Denver's secondary and allows defensive coordinator Vance Joseph to build his game plans around having a premier corner capable of limiting an opponent's top receiving threat.

Now, Denver will have to find a different way to defend Seattle's most dangerous offensive weapon.

Smith-Njigba has been one of the NFL's most productive receivers this season, and his production has continued even while dealing with an ankle issue. He was listed as a limited participant for the second consecutive day Tuesday, but he finished Seattle's Week 5 loss to San Francisco with five catches for 102 yards and a touchdown.

Broncos secondary takes another major hit

Nov 30, 2025; Landover, Maryland, USA; Denver Broncos cornerback Pat Surtain II (2) tackles Washington Commanders tight end Zach Ertz (86) in the first quarter of the game at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Peter Casey-Imagn Images

The Surtain news is even more concerning because Denver won't have its full complement of defensive backs. Safety Talanoa Hufanga has also been ruled out and is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury.

Cornerback Riley Moss is listed as questionable after missing last week's game with a rib injury, although he has returned to limited participation this week.

That leaves Denver potentially facing Seattle without two of its most important defensive backs while trying to slow down Smith-Njigba and an offense that has shown the ability to create explosive plays through the air.

The Broncos managed to beat the Chargers last week despite Surtain's absence, but Seattle presents a very different challenge. Smith-Njigba is playing at an elite level, and losing Surtain removes Denver's best option for making life difficult for the Seahawks' star receiver.

articles.title: Bengals rank near NFL's bottom in play-action usage through Week 5
articles.summary: The Bengals are using play action on just 12.2% of their offensive snaps this season, the second-lowest rate in the NFL.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals have a supremely talented NFL passing attack, but they are an outlier in how rarely they use play action.

Per Sharp Football Analysis , Cincinnati has used play action on just 12.2% of its offensive snaps this season. That ranks 31st among 32 teams, ahead of only the Philadelphia Eagles at 10.4%.

The New Orleans Saints are next at 12.3%, while no other team sits below 12.9%.

It continues a trend from last season. Pro Football Focus noted that Cincinnati used play action at a 17.1% rate in 2025, well below the NFL average of 25.65%.

Despite that tendency, Joe Burrow and the Bengals offense have produced. Cincinnati comes into its Week 6 bye at 3-2 while averaging 25.6 points per game. Burrow threw four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.

Regardless, the play-action number is an evident offensive tendency to evaluate during the bye before an AFC North matchup with the Baltimore Ravens in Week 7.

articles.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur seems to be in dire straits in the desert
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur has not delivered the dynamic turnaround, but he must assume responsibility for recent let downs.
articles.body:
The underwhelming statistical output the Arizona Cardinals have yielded for throughout the first five games of the NFL season has been quite dismal. Furthermore, fans and critics may begin to contemplate whether team administration made the right decision by hiring first-year head coach Mike LaFleur.

LaFleur wasn't the primary choice nor too candidate but was a secondary option after the Las Vegas Raiders hired Klint Kubiak as their head coach earlier this year. LaFleur's repertoire didn't have a hefty acclaim but his connection and operative role as an assistant to Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay did summon him some favor. LaFleur also spent a few years with the New York Jets and other franchises as well. Still, operating as a head coach in the NFL takes a certain leadership quality that has not really been exemplified by LaFleur in the first five games. A combination of team turnovers, lack of discipline, penalties and utter offensive indecision in strategy all seem to mirror the novice disposition of LaFleur who quite frankly has not showed himself to be competent so far.

Many Cardinals' fans question whether or not defensive coordinator Nick Rallis should've been retained but an analytical deeper look shows that the Arizona Cardinals offense has been quite counterproductive. Thus without an ability to sustain offensive drives, A area facet that the newly head coach was supposed to edify, It's very difficult not to share some spotlight on LaFleur and his shortcomings.

articles.title: Bills' Joe Brady Clarifies Viral Comments on James Cook Losing Playing Time Amid Fumbling Issues
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady clarified comments from Tuesday saying he would consider decreasing James Cook's carries if he didn't lessen his fumbles, telling reporters a day later he still intends to feed the star running back the ball.
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady clarified comments from Tuesday saying he would consider decreasing James Cook's carries if he didn't lessen his fumbles, telling reporters a day later he still intends to feed the star running back the ball.

"I don't want James running any more timid," he said. "He's playing outstanding right now, in terms of how he's running the football. I don't know if anyone is running the ball better than him in the NFL. But we're putting the ball on the ground. And so there's a fine line in terms of, I don't want him feeling like he has to be scared of how he's running, and now he's not hitting the hole. ... He's aware of it, we're going to continue coaching it. But I don't want you guys to think I'm going to stop giving Cook the ball either."

Cook had two fumbles during Monday night's win over the Los Angeles Rams, losing one in overtime that gave the Rams the ball with a chance to win (though Buffalo blocked a field goal on L.A.'s ensuing possession). He now has four fumbles this season and 11 dating back to the 2025 campaign, including the playoffs.

But he's also third in the NFL in rushing yards (532) and is one of Buffalo's most dynamic offensive weapons, so the ideal solution isn't benching him. But there's little doubt that his ball security needs to improve.

articles.title: Kellen Moore Responds to Warning from Saints Owner amid 1-4 Start to NFL Season
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore reacted to being called out by team owner Gayle Benson after compiling a 1-4 record to begin the 2026 season.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore reacted to being called out by team owner Gayle Benson after compiling a 1-4 record to begin the 2026 season.

"It's where we're at," Moore said Wednesday, via Josh Alper of Pro Football Talk. "We're 1-4, missed a few opportunities right there. We all want the same thing. We're all shooting for that. We've all got the same objectives and we just gotta get better moving forward."

After the Saints suffered a 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 5, Benson issued a warning to Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis.

4 Arrested in February Shooting of 49ers' Keion White

"Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform," Benson said Tuesday, per NOLA.com's Rod Walker and Matthew Paras . "Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."

The Saints wrapped up a 6-11 finish in 2025, but won four of their final five games and were looking to take a step forward this season with an offense led by second-year quarterback Tyler Shough and free-agent addition Travis Etienne.

New Orleans' defense has struggled mightily, ranking No. 31 among all teams by allowing 30.2 points per game. The Saints have also given up 361.0 total yards on a weekly basis.

While Moore's offense is averaging a modest 23.6 points per game, issues will ball security have prevented the unit from overcoming the team's defensive woes. New Orleans has committed 11 turnovers, tied for the second-most in the league.

The Saints will attempt to get back on track in Week 6, as they'll face off against a New York Giants squad that has opened the year with a 3-1-1 record.

articles.title: Caleb Williams' return should solve many of the Bears' problems, but young pass-catchers still have work to do
articles.summary: Matt Harmon puts the Bears under the microscope to see what getting Caleb Williams back will mean for the team and fantasy managers.
articles.body:
At the close of fantasy draft season this summer, the Chicago Bears had five players in the top 70 overall. So far, only D'Andre Swift drafters are remotely happy with that. Even with some bumps lately, he's still the RB12 in points per game after being drafted as the RB19 in Round 4.

Neither Luther Burden nor Rome Odunze at wide receiver has consistently made a difference, and tight end Colston Loveland at 38th overall is arguably the worst pick on the board through five weeks.

In general, I don't want to make any sweeping conclusions or grand pronouncements about this group of pass-catchers until we get a more extended view of how everything sorts out when Chicago has its starting quarterback.

Caleb Williams has played one full game this season; the Bears scored 59 points in that contest while Williams looked like an evolved version of his 2025 self. He didn't put the ball in harm's way, kept the offense on schedule, and took shot plays when available but opted for checkdowns and layups when they weren't. The Bears were the best offense in the NFL in Week 1 and even if the run game was awesome and Williams was excellent as a scrambler, they boasted the fourth-best success rate on passing plays. Williams operated as the type of quarterback most of his detractors insist he simply will never be in the NFL in that win.

Things fell apart in Week 2 when the team played against Brian Flores and the NFL's No. 1-ranked defense — by a long shot based on EPA per play and success rate allowed — in a rainstorm. Williams didn't finish the game after suffering a hamstring injury after playing 87% of the snaps.

In a tale as old as time, the backup quarterbacks played well in each of their respective first starts in a well-designed Ben Johnson offense but haven't sustained that momentum because they can't push the ball downfield. This is best expressed in the Bears ranking 20th in explosive play rate through five weeks, after finishing seventh in 2025. They are still eighth in explosive rushing rate, so the pass game is the bigger anchor here.

In Weeks 3 to 5, they ranked 28th in explosive play rate overall but first in time of possession per drive. If you've watched Ben Johnson offenses, you know he prioritizes explosive plays, not just holding onto and moving the ball. This has been their biggest issue.

The return of their uber-talented young quarterback who can attack every blade of grass should solve most of this. But how much will it move the needle for each individual player? That's what we'll look into in this space.

We should acknowledge that the Bears are not one of the most concentrated passing trees in the NFL. They are one of 10 teams with five or more players who own a 10% target share. Their top two players (Luther Burden III and Rome Odunze) combine for a 39.5% target share; that's the 12th-lowest for a top duo among all NFL teams.

No one projected Kalif Raymond to finish the first five weeks with a 16.7% target share and 14.5% air yard share, both of which rank third on the team. He's really complicated the distribution and has siphoned layup targets away from the supposed top-three players. Now, his designed plays were quite effective in Weeks 1 to 3 but have gone nowhere the last two games (12 yards on six targets). His route participation has also dipped below 60%; his role may be shrinking, which wouldn't be a massive shock for a 32-year-old veteran role player. If he sticks around, it'll make the margin for error even tighter for the three young mainstays.

Burden has been the biggest victim of the offense's lack of explosive plays. His average depth of completion is below 7 yards.

So far, the Bears haven't been able to activate him outside of designer targets close to the line of scrimmage. Without a doubt, there have been plays on dig in-breaking routes where he's gotten open the last few weeks, and the ball just doesn't find him. There were several examples in Week 5 with Tyson Bagent under center.

Those were the mainstays in Burden's route diet as a rookie and where he's meant to be most useful to the Bears offense as an explosive player.

I'm confident Williams, who hit Burden on a few of these exact routes in Week 1 against Carolina, will be able to get the ball here better than Bagent or Case Keenum.

The issue for Burden to date, and it's still early in Year 2, is that neither his role nor play style has expanded from his rookie season. Burden has not run a route on 80% or more of the dropbacks in any game this season. He's run a route on only 39% of dropbacks when there are two or fewer receivers on the field. You can be the most efficient player in the league but it's quite hard to be a productive player week-in-week-out when that's your role.

That needs to change for Burden to hit the ceiling his ADP suggested this summer. He needs to come close to completely removing Raymond from the rotation to get there. The problem is that I don't think he's winning on enough real-deal receiver routes to push the veteran or command more downfield looks overall. The plays where he gets open are there; they just need to happen more consistently. I would have said the same thing about his rookie season and college tape.

I still remain a fan of Burden's game overall and am not writing him off whatsoever. Getting Williams back under center will help his weekly ceiling outcomes. He just needs to take a few more steps forward to lift his floor. If and when he does, his play style and deployment make it easy for quarterbacks to find him and get him the ball to run after the catch.

Odunze has not consistently popped off either but for almost the exact opposite reasons as Burden.

Odunze has no playing time issues. He's run a route on 82% of the dropbacks with two or fewer receivers on the field from Weeks 2 to 5 after he was a part-time player in the season opener. He has had no issues getting open at all levels of the field. Odunze has become one of the best route runners and separators in the NFL. It's quite easy to see on tape.

The problem, from a pure production standpoint, is that he plays the highest-difficulty role in the wide receiver room. His average depth of route is 10.7 yards downfield, per Fantasy Points Data, while everyone else on the team is below 8.0. He doesn't get the same layup crossers or quick slants that go the way of Burden or Raymond. While he is not a sacrificial X-receiver, he does take the most snaps outside and on-ball on the team. He doesn't run an above-average rate of go routes (15%) but his primary route diet comes from big posts, digs and corners.

Odunze is excellent on those patterns and they are critical to the team hitting the explosive plays that Johnson so desires to make the base of his offense. Yet, that role has a ton of variance, regardless of how good a player might be in isolation. We've seen that in just the last two games. When the quarterback is protected and playing on time, as Bagent was in Week 4, the X-receiver can be the primary target and be the reason his team thrives in the passing game. When things go a bit more awry, as they certainly did in Week 5, that player can come away with 3-40 even when they lead the team in targets.

If we're calling balls and strikes here, Odunze has also made some of his own problems the last two seasons with big mistakes at critical times. Some of that is overstated this year, as he has only one drop — a particularly disgusting one in the end zone in Week 3 in an island game — and sports the best contested-catch rate on the team of 75%, per Fantasy Points Data. Still, in a crowded offense in a low-percentage role, you need to make the most of every opportunity.

Odunze's role as the vertical X-receiver definitely needs a quarterback like Williams to thrive. He is the most susceptible to chaos. Even still, Odunze doesn't play in the most "fantasy-friendly" role and that will lead to volatility; even more so if Williams suffers bouts of inaccuracy that haunted him in 2024 and 2025 when throwing downfield. I remain bullish on their connection but I could see this being a similar situation to another elite separator, Brandon Aiyuk, when he was the downfield X-receiver for the 2022 and 2023 49ers with tons of other layup options on the team. Aiyuk didn't crack 110 targets in 2023 but cleared 1,300 yards because he was outrageously efficient in a good ecosystem.

Odunze needs to clean up some areas of his game to reach that final, long-shot level and it definitely won't happen either way without the version of Williams we saw in Week 1.

Loveland is maybe the trickiest one to figure out — a shame considering he was the earliest drafted player of the bunch. Right now, he's fourth on the team in both targets and air yards. No one signed up for that. Raymond's presence has been a big hindrance to his outlook, as they run routes in similar areas of the field. Loveland has just one game with a target share north of 14%. It came in Week 4 when Raymond had a season-low 6% target share … that's not a coincidence.

In Week 1, Loveland ran a route on 89.5% of the dropbacks, even if he didn't catch a pass. Since then, his route participation has been below 77% in every game. In his dominant stretch as the clear leading player in the Bears passing game from Week 16 through the playoffs, Loveland ran a route in 81% of dropbacks and was targeted on 30.5% of those pass patterns. We just aren't seeing anything close to that usage right now.

One of Loveland's superpowers in that stretch was his ability to play out-wide as a mismatch option. He averaged 3.08 yards per route run lined up outside in that five-game stretch, totaling 154 yards and 12 catches on 20 targets. So far, this season, he's caught just three passes for 25 yards on six targets in five games when lined up out-wide. He caught all of his passes in Week 4.

To my eye test, he hasn't looked as explosive or fluid as a separator on those reps in particular through the first five weeks as he did in the back half of his rookie season. That is a small sample and could just be a blip. It's just one explanation for why he hasn't popped in this role. His air yards per target on his looks outside is 7.5, well south of his five-game stretch from Week 16 through the playoffs last year (10.2). He just hasn't been getting the same chunky downfield looks in those advantageous spots as we saw in 2025. It's easy to tell yourself a convincing story that this changes with Williams back in the mix.

My other theory, in addition to simple variance and a small-sample slump, as to why Loveland's production is down is that it's not an uncommon issue for tight end production; he's blocking more often. For the Bears offense, this isn't a bad thing at all. Loveland is one of the best blocking tight ends among full-time starters who are also, in theory, highly dangerous pass-catchers.

In the run game, Loveland is a weapon. That he isn't a defensive tell and is also a mismatch weapon as a receiver is what made him special last year.

However, so far in 2026, he's stayed in to pass block on 13.2% of his snaps, way up from 5.8% overall in 2025 and in the Week 16 to Divisional Round run rate of 3.9%. Again, this is helpful to the Bears' offense. Williams isn't the only starter the team is currently missing. Chicago has played the start of the season without left tackle Ozzy Trapilo, who was fantastic as a rookie but tore his patellar tendon in the 2025 postseason. The team rotated Braxton Jones and Theo Benedet at left tackle around their four other stalwart starters before Jones went on IR. Benedet is an athletic mover in the run game but leaky in pass protection. It makes sense for Loveland to have to help out until Trapilo returns.

Even in plays with three or more receivers on the field, Loveland has pass-blocked on 14% of his plays and has run a route on only 70% of the team's total dropbacks. These may seem like small shifts but from a pure production and much less fantasy standpoint, these make all the difference on the margins for tight ends. It's even more true when a passing tree is more crowded than expected, as is clearly the case in Chicago.

If Trapilo, who is on the active roster, dresses for game day here soon, we still need to see if he can get back to form in short order. If he does, it could free Loveland up to run more routes and be deployed as a pass-catcher. There's also a chance that this is how Loveland will help his team this year as Trapilo returns from a serious injury, which may take time to get back to 100%. That would be a big boost for a Bears offense that's destined to rise in the ranks the moment Williams returns. It just won't move the needle for Loveland's depressed fantasy outlook.

Ultimately, I'm still buying on Colston Loveland as a long-term talent, just as I am on both of his young wide receiver teammates, Luther Burden and Rome Odunze. Aside from a few individual critiques, backup-quarterback influence and shifting external factors have largely shaped the box-score results for all three players. We know the quarterback is returning soon, and likely this week, which will undoubtedly help. The question is just how much it moves the needle for all three of these talented players, and all of them have at least one other quandary that needs solving, beyond Williams getting back under center.

articles.title: Rams tackle Alaric Jackson wins appeal, will miss just one game for punching Bills' Bradley Chubb

articles.title: Mike Tomlin offers blunt take on NFL players-only meetings: ‘I think you’re dead’
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin told Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on "New Heights" that the Dallas Cowboys' reported players-only meeting is a very troubling sign.
articles.body: The Dallas Cowboys’ uneven start continued in Week 5, when they fell to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and dropped to 2-3 through five games. Against that backdrop, the Cowboys reportedly held a players-only meeting. Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach and current NBC Sports NFL analyst Mike Tomlin offered his perspective on what a players-only meeting can signal about a team’s state of affairs. MIKE TOMLIN'S COACH CRITICISM MAKES HIM BETTER TV ANALYST BUT RAISES QUESTION WHETHER HE'S EYEING COWBOYS JOB "I think you’re dead," Tomlin told ESPN’s Jason Kelce and Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce, during the latest episode of the brothers’ "New Heights" podcast. JERRY JONES GOES ALL IN AS COWBOYS TRADE FOR STEELERS' JOEY PORTER JR IN HOPES OF SUPER BOWL PUSH Jason Kelce’s visible support for the Philadelphia Eagles during broadcasts has drawn attention since he retired from the only team he played for and moved into broadcasting. Travis Kelce then asked whether Tomlin had faced criticism for speaking fondly of the Steelers during "Football Night in America" broadcasts. articles.title: "A deal could happen any time”: Tyreek Hill’s agent breaks silence on his future as the star wide receiver remains without a team

articles.body: Tyreek Hill, the former Miami Dolphins’ wide receiver, has remained without a team ever since he was released after he sustained brutal injuries in the last season. On top of that, the star player has also been involved in a controversial lawsuit with his estranged wife Keeta Vaccaro as she filed for divorce and accused him of domestic violence. Amid all the mess, Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus has now weighed in on what can be expected in the ongoing season.Tyreek Hill’s agent weighs in on his future in the league as he remains without a team in the ongoing seasonA few hours ago, in an interview withJosh Moser, Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said,"You know, Josh, I think it's very fluid. I think a deal could happen any time. We are looking for the right situation, the right contract, the right team, the right fit, the right approach from a medical standpoint. Tyreek's feeling really good health-wise. I did say last week I thought a deal could happen at any time. But in the NFL, it really is day-to-day. So we are still working to find the right situation. "Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus added, “Well, you know, when you sign with the team midseason, you'd like to go to a winner. Number two, as a wide receiver, you'd like to go to a team that needs a wide receiver. Number three, you'd like to go to a team that's got a pretty good quarterback. And number four, Tyreek's going to bring a lot of impact. We've got to get a fair contract.”He continued, “And that's always complex to negotiate in the middle of the season. articles.title: 'Week From Hell,' Eagles OT Opens Up amid Emotional Stretch, 3-Game Losing Streak
articles.summary: Last week was more than a little eventful for the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Last week was more than a little eventful for the Philadelphia Eagles.

Future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson retired; interior offensive lineman Cam Jurgens was traded to the Baltimore Ravens; the Eagles dealt with a number of injuries to key players; and the team had to travel to London to face the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, losing on a walk-off field-goal after Nick Sirianni's debatable decision to not go for a touchback on the kick-off one play prior.

4 Arrested in February Shooting of 49ers' Keion White

"My brain hurts," left tackle Jordan Mailata told reporters on Monday when asked if Philly's field-goal drive late in the fourth quarter, after a number of offensive struggles this season, provided any sense of a moral victory. "This week has been a week from hell for me. I don't even know the concept of a moral victory right now. I'm just trying to look internally to see how I contributed to this loss so I can correct it. We weren't good enough. We know that."

The Eagles are now 2-3 and mired in a three-game losing streak, largely down to an offense that ranks 29th in scoring (18.4 PPG) and 31st in yards (262.2 YPG). Injuries to a number of key players like Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Landon Dickerson at various points this season hasn't helped, and the loss of Johnson will be massive. But Mailata is holding out hope that the Birds can turn things around.

"I'm actually very excited and very high on the team right now," he said Monday. "Because I think defense picked us up, not just on the field but with everything we went through this week, they picked us up off the field. We did link arms and I think moving forward, we're linking arms even more now. There's no blame to be tossed around. Again, it's how can I do my 1/11th and how can I contribute to a win? Unfortunately, we lost so now it's how did my 1/11th contribute to the loss? And that's how we have to look at it. There are moments in the game that we all want back and we all contributed. It's tough."

articles.body:
The two-game suspension for Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for punching Buffalo Bills linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face has been reduced to one upon appeal.

The NFL announced the decision Wednesday . The decision to reduce the suspension was made by hearing officer Derrick Brooks, who was jointly appointed by the NFL and NFLPA. No reason for the decision was provided.

Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals, but he will now be eligible to face the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7. Backup David Quessenberry is slated to start Sunday in Jackson's absence. Quessenberry's made 30 NFL starts, but none since the 2023 season with the Minnesota Vikings.

Chubb reveals what he said to set Jackson off

The NFL initially announced a two-game suspension for Jackson on Tuesday, hours after he was caught on camera punching Chubb in the face on the SoFi Stadium field in the aftermath of "Monday Night Football." Chubb's Bills beat Jackson's Rams, 37-34, in a dramatic overtime game in Los Angeles.

Jackson was exchanging his jersey with a Bills player when Chubb started chirping at him.

Chubb then turned around and walked away. Jackson followed Chubb, and the two exchanged words. Jackson then punched Chubb in the face. Chubb's teammates then pulled him away.

At Bills practice Wednesday, Chubb revealed his side of the story about what he said to Jackson. Per ESPN :

"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. "I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' "He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all.

"I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.'

"He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

Jackson hasn't spoken in public about the punch or the suspension.

Monday's loss dropped a Rams team that was a preseason Super Bowl favorite to 2-3. The loss of their most important offensive lineman to suspension provided another blow to an already difficult season that was softened by Wednesday's news.

The Rams are hoping to get on track with winnable games against the Cardinals, Raiders, Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals again prior to a Week 11 bye.

articles.title: Bradley Chubb Reveals What He Said to Alaric Jackson Before Punch After Bills' MNF Win vs. Rams
articles.summary: After an altercation with Los Angeles Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson on Monday, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb broke down the incident from his perspective.
articles.body:
After an altercation with Los Angeles Rams offensive tackle Alaric Jackson on Monday, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb broke down the incident from his perspective.

Chubb dispelled rumors that he discussed Jackson's mom and said he was instead keeping his trash talk about the game.

"I'll tell you exactly what I said," Chubb told reporters Wednesday. "I've heard I was talking about his mom. That's not true at all. I said, 'We're gonna see y'all's ass again. And when we see you again, all that chipping ain't gonna save you. That tight end and guard is not going to save you.' He said, 'What'd you say?' I said, 'That chip's not gonna save you. The guard's not gonna save you.' And then boom."

Chubb and Jackson exchanged words after the game and Jackson struck Chubb in the face. He was initially suspended for two games, but the suspension was later reduced to just one game.

The Rams will be without Jackson for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.

Chubb said that he started the conversation with Jackson and was upset by the Rams' demeanor when it seemed like they had the game in the bag. Specifically, Chubb said he felt Los Angeles was "front-running."

The Rams had the ball in field goal position in overtime after Buffalo fumbled on its opening drive, but the Bills blocked Harrison Mevis' game-winning field goal attempt.

Led by the legs of quarterback Josh Allen, Buffalo marched down the field to make a field goal to seal the overtime victory, 37-34. Chubb logged two tackles in the win.

"It was an emotional game. Tempers got flared," Chubb told reporters after the game. "But it is what it is. We flushed it and we onto next week."

While Chubb acknowledges that he started the incident, he also said that he was proud of the way he responded, not punching back and potentially risking a suspension of his own.

Still, it was a learning moment for Chubb and his teammates.

"We're going to learn from it," Chubb said. "Me personally, I learned I'm either going to have my hands up or wear a helmet."

articles.summary: Terry Bradshaw was not looking for a new relationship when he met Tammy in a Texas hospital in 2003.
articles.body: Terry Bradshaw was not looking for a new relationship when he met Tammy in a Texas hospital in 2003. The former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback had been through three divorces and was trying to focus on his mental health. Then an injured horse trainer brought him to Baylor Scott & White Medical Center in Grapevine, where Tammy was working in radiology. Their first meeting sparked an immediate attraction, but dating a famous NFL figure was another matter. Even after a successful first date, Tammy questioned whether she was ready for the life that came with him.Terry Bradshaw’s hospital encounter with Tammy led to an unexpected first dateBradshaw, now 78, accompanied a horse trainer from his ranch to the hospital for an X-ray after the trainer broke an ankle. That was where he first saw Tammy, then a radiology manager and educator.“They had to X-ray [the trainer’s broken ankle],” he recounts to PEOPLE from the kitchen table at the couple’s horse breeding ranch in Saint Jo, Texas, last month. “And through the doors comes blondie. I went, ‘Oh my God, is she ever more gorgeous?’ I automatically said, ‘Oh, wow.’ “Bradshaw tried to strike up a conversation while Tammy focused on her work. She remembers the exchange with humor, saying, “I’m just trying to do my job.”Still, the attraction was not one-sided. Tammy recalls making eye contact with the former quarterback and being struck by his eyes. “He looked at me and we made eye contact. And it’s just like in a movie, the thought that went through my brain was, ‘This man has the bluest eyes I’ve ever seen in my life. I can see all the way to his soul,’ “ she says.Tammy initially thought little more of the encounter than a memorable meeting with a local celebrity. That changed when Bradshaw left her a voicemail she described as the “most unassuming, sweet voicemail.” He had obtained her number through an acquaintance who worked at the hospital.She was nervous about accepting his invitation because of his fame, but the first date went well. “I had such a good time with him and I could tell he was a good person.”Tammy’s hesitation came as Terry Bradshaw faced doubts about marriageA good first date did not settle Tammy’s concerns. Bradshaw kept calling, but she often let the phone ring. The question was whether she felt ready to enter a relationship with someone whose life was so different from hers.“He kept calling and I kept not answering the phone. I was going, ‘Can I do this?’ ... He’s in a whole different world. ‘Am I confident enough to even think about entering this situation?’ “ she says.Her daughter, Lacey Hester, now 37, encouraged her to give the relationship a chance. Tammy and Bradshaw went on to date for more than a decade before marrying in 2014. They renewed their vows in 2021.Their long courtship was not without setbacks. Bradshaw continued to struggle with fears linked to his previous marriages and divorces. At times, he pulled away, once ending the relationship through an email. The separation lasted months.“I would get scared,” he admits. “I didn’t trust myself, honestly.”Tammy said she understood that Bradshaw, who lives with clinical depression, was working to find the right treatment plan, including medication. She chose not to pressure him into making decisions before he was ready.“I learned to stand still and he would always come back,” she says.Looking back, Bradshaw believes those personal struggles ultimately brought them together. “Personal struggles is what got me to her,” he reflects. “If it hadn’t been for this, it couldn’t have been that.”The couple now speak openly about how fortunate they feel to have found each other. articles.title: Netflix's 'Untold' series to drop new documentary on the Daejon Love/49ers scandal
articles.summary: Netflix announced that "Untold: Wide Deceiver" will be released in the near future.
articles.body:
The Daejon Love scandal is coming to Netflix.

The streaming giant announced plans Wednesday for a new documentary featuring the man who allegedly portrayed himself as a San Francisco 49ers player to defraud several women out of more than $1.3 million.

It's unclear when the documentary, which is part of the "Untold" series and will be titled "Wide Deceiver," will be released. But the story, Netflix said, is going to be told firsthand by Love's accusers and "will unpack the internet nickname and the far darker story it exposed."

Love, 35, was arrested in August alongside 18-year-old Taylor Chan in the scandal. The duo were charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. Officials said that Love repeatedly posed as a 49ers player or a wealthy real estate investor for years, and that the pair targeted women through dating apps to eventually defraud them out of money. Victims sent them money with the intent that it would be deployed for fruitful investments, prosecutors said.

Initially, officials said the pair had exploited 26 people of more than $1.3 million across California, Idaho, Washington and Oregon. Last month, however, federal investigators said they had identified an additional 35 women who said they were defrauded by Love and Chan, and they believe there are more victims out there.

One woman, Gwen Herndon, said she even reached out to the 49ers about Love in December, about eight months before he was arrested. She wrote a message through the team's "complaint/concern" form submission. Herndon filed a lawsuit against Love in small claims civil court in Oregon last year after she said she gave Love $10,000 for an investment. Once she started asking questions and for her money back, she said Love blocked her.

The "Untold" series has been around for years now, and started with a documentary on the infamous "Malice and the Palace" brawl between the Indiana Pacers and Detroit Pistons in 2004. The series has covered a variety of topics throughout sports.

Even though Love was arrested only a few months ago, Netflix is moving fast here. But with how the Daejon Love story spread on social media after the scandal was revealed, it's easy to see why.

articles.title: Will Jets rookie David Bailey's ascent continue vs. Patriots, Drake Maye? 'You guys tell me'
articles.summary: The Jets' No. 2 overall pick is off to a torrid start to his career, including a historic three-sacks performance last week. What does he have in store for a...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — In the aftermath of the New York Jets' win on Sunday over the Cleveland Browns, head coach Aaron Glenn was asked about his rookie pass rusher.

What did Glenn think of the 2026 second overall draft pick's performance?

"You guys tell me," Glenn said, knowing there was little up for debate.

Bailey rushed from the left and from the right, bull-rushing his way to quarterback Deshaun Watson on some plays and spinning out of attempted blockers on others.

The result: nine pressures, five quick pressures and a 32.1% pressure rate, per Next Gen Stats. Bailey's three sacks tied a 1995 record for the most in a game by a Jets rookie since sacks were tracked in 1982. His five sacks this season are tied for fourth in the NFL and first among rookies.

"Just relentless," Glenn told reporters on Monday. "The same things you really saw from him coming out of college. His ability to bend the edge, his ability to dip, lean, use power in that lean and be able to rip up and be able to go make plays on the quarterback. His ability to make a move and then rush with power also. The other things that really showed up in the game was his ability to play the run, and I think that's one thing that he's not getting enough credit for …

"He just had an all-around game as far as affecting the quarterback and playing the run."

The Jets and Bailey now turn their attention to a road division game against a quarterback who narrowly lost the MVP race last season to Matthew Stafford. The Jets face New England Patriots QB Drake Maye right after he torched the Las Vegas Raiders for 374 yards and four touchdowns passing in addition to 25 yards and a touchdown rushing. Maye completed a season-high 76.5% of his passes vs. the Raiders.

Can Bailey and Co. stem that tide, or even force some of the turnovers that characterized Maye's first three games this season?

Glenn's advice to the Jets about defending a flight-risk Watson apply to the also extremely mobile Maye.

"Listen, I'll sit there and be lying to our guys [if I] say that he wasn't going to make a play," Glenn said. "At some point, he's going to get out. That's just what good players do. But I think the guys respect that I don't BS them and tell them, listen, he's going to get out every now and then, but the thing is we got to make sure that we trap him inside. And if we can trap him inside, there's a chance that we're going to be able to make some plays. …

"If we could just limit his chance of getting out, I think we'll create some success for ourselves on defense."

Bailey was disruptive from both sides vs. Browns

In four prior career games against the Jets, Maye has completed 73.9% of his pass attempts for 582 yards and six touchdowns, rushing also for 82 yards and a score.

The Jets drafted Bailey to help turn the tides in just such games.

A one-year edge rusher at Texas Tech after three seasons at Stanford, Bailey's first-step quickness and explosiveness flashed during his lone year in Lubbock. Rushing every down, rather than the hybrid rush and coverage role he filled at Stanford, produced an FBS-best 14.5 sacks last year. He also added 52 tackles, 19.5 tackles for loss, three pass deflections, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery.

The Jets are leaning into his first-step quickness while also looking to maximize his versatility.

Bailey lined up at right outside linebacker on his first of nine quarterback pressures against Watson, bull-rushing left tackle Spencer Fano, drafted seven picks after Bailey, before he swallowed Watson as the quarterback tried to pick up a snap that had slipped from his hands on a rainy day.

Bailey then settled back in from the left side throughout the game, overpowering opponents ranging from right tackle Dawand Jones to tight ends Harold Fannin Jr. and Blake Whiteheart on different snaps to flush Watson from the pocket on a missed end-zone strike in the second quarter, speed up a 30-yard completion to Isaiah Bond on an early fourth-quarter attempt, and trip Watson as he threw it away late in the fourth.

In concert with fellow Jets rushers and Glenn's blitz-heavy game plan, New York pressured Watson on 59.1% of his passes, 14.3% more than his previous season high vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars and nearly triple the 21.6% rate he'd faced a week earlier from the Steelers.

Bailey credited his study and his teammates.

"Just working together with my D line, also the linebackers, understanding what pressures are being called, where the pressures are coming from and how that affects my approach to my rush," Bailey said. "So I think just understanding the defense as a whole and rushing together with our rush-lane integrity."

Bailey could face a depleted Patriots offensive line.

Starting left tackle Will Campbell sustained a knee injury that limited him to 28 snaps vs. the Raiders, rookie first-rounder Caleb Lomu playing 49 snaps in relief. Starting right tackle Morgan Moses is also battling a foot injury that limited him in Wednesday practice but he did not miss time.

Maye and Co. will keep an eye out for Bailey.

"He's fast, explosive, instinctive," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said. "He can bend, got a really good get-off and is able to win at the top and corner. He uses his get-off, so just like every week, we'll have to be very conscious of the front. They do a nice job interior-wise. They're big, they're physical. Then on the edges, they can create some havoc. I think when they blitz, they have a really good blitz demeanor, whether it's [Jamien] Sherwood, Demario Davis or [Jarvis] Brownlee.

"They've been able to just create disruption when they blitz."

The decision to prioritize edge rusher at the second overall pick reflected the Jets' team life cycle as well as the divisional reality of the AFC East.

A team that can't stop Maye will be hard-pressed to beat the Patriots. A team that can't stop Josh Allen best beware the Buffalo Bills. (The Miami Dolphins are earlier in their rebuild than the Jets.)

Bailey showed flashes in his first four games, averaging half a sack and 2.75 pressures per game in that stretch. In his 54 snaps against the Browns, his three tackles for loss tied his four-game prior mark.

Will competing against a quarterback with a deeper track record of recent success prove the chance for Bailey to show what he's capable of this week, or a reminder that facing the Browns in poor weather conditions complicates a quarterback's execution?

Will Maye's next outing reflect the top-tier quarterback play of his last two weeks or the rhythmic lapses and turnovers of his first three?

"We really don't focus on what happened in the past when it comes to us, we just focus on what's happening right now," Glenn said. "But yes, division games are definitely crucial. Sometimes people say they count as two games, but the only thing that we're focused on is this is the one game that we have to play, this is the one game we want to win, this is the one game that we're prepared for and look to win.

"So, good team, a team that was in the Super Bowl last year, and we're going to look forward to playing them."

articles.title: “Put Him on the Bench”: Ex-NFL QB Asks Titans to Make a Stern Decision on Cam Ward’s Development Amid Growing Criticism

articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are having a dismal 2026 run so far, going winless across the first five weeks. Titans quarterback Cam Ward, in particular, received much criticism for his performance in his sophomore season in the league, leading critics to call for his removal from the starting QB role. One former NFL quarterback, who believes Ward has the potential to develop, feels that being benched wouldn't be a bad thing.

While discussing the Titans' predicament on the Fitz & Whit podcast , former quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick felt that the Tennessee team should bench Ward for the time being and use veteran backup Mitchell Trubisky to give the younger QB a chance to work on himself.

"I actually believe in Cam Ward. … I think the best thing for his development is to put him on the bench for the next few games," Fitzpatrick said. "Guess what? I've been in this situation plenty. It's going to provide him a different perspective. He's going to be able to take a step back, he's going to get to watch somebody else operate in offense.

"Mitchell Trubisky, so, a 10-year vet, a guy that's going to go in, you're just going to see it from a different perspective. You're going to be able to pull back, but it's also, it's going to give you some time to work on yourself."

Ward, the No. 1 pick of the 2025 draft, didn't get much time to develop his skills. In his first season as a starter, he went 3-14. While his first year could be excused since he was only a rookie, there was an expectation that Ward would be able to clean up in his second year.

But in 2026, Ward completed just 98 of 155 pass attempts for 896 yards and three touchdowns. Analysts have noted inconsistencies in his technique, particularly his footwork issues and how unsettled he seems when the pocket breaks down. According to The Tennesseans Mike Organ, Ward has one of the lowest NFL completion rates under pressure at 36.6%.

Fitzpatrick also spoke of his own experience of being benched by the Texans back in 2014. He insisted that the two games he spent watching backup QB Ryan Mallett play gave him a lot of valuable insight into which aspects of his own game needed polishing. Mallett went 1-1 as the starter, and was replaced by Fitzpatrick after suffering a chest injury.

The Titans QB, however, is committed to doing better.

"No, I'm not a loser," Ward said after the loss to the Houston Texans after being asked if he had become used to losing. "The record may say that we are right now. But at the end of the day, you have got to go through some stuff to try to get wins.

"We attack this each and every day, but for that, if you're able to look at everyone in our locker room's track record, we've all won games at a high level, and we're looking forward to doing that in the long run."

The Titans have a new head coach in Robert Saleh, and a new offensive coordinator in Brian Daboll. This is the second time in as many years Ward has had to learn a new system, which could also be playing a part in the QB not being able to tap into his potential.

The former NFL star believes benching Ward will not only give the Titans, who are still looking for their first win, the support of a veteran, but also give Ward time to understand exactly where he's struggling and hopefully trigger a similarly dramatic improvement in his performance.

In the post-game conference after the loss to the Texans, Ward was also asked why he deserved to be the team's long-term answer at QB. His answer carried some weight.

"I just think my process," Ward said. "… I love the criticism. I love everything that comes with the quarterback territory. At the end of the day, it's the best position in the world. Stuff goes the right way, you take all the credit. Stuff goes the wrong way, you take all the blame.

"I know I'm capable of this position. I have the right guys around me to uplift me and myself to uplift them, and we're going to put it together eventually."

It is high time he lives up to these claims.

articles.title: Former Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. opens up about Houston move after Arizona exit

articles.body:
HOUSTON — For the first time since his trade to the Houston Texans, former Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. spoke to reporters Wednesday about the move.

Arizona Cardinals receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18) looks back at quarterback Jacoby Brissett (7) against the Seattle Seahawks during a game at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz. on Sept. 20, 2026. Credit: Patrick Breen/The Republic / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

The blockbuster trade was first reported Saturday, though details about the package and which team would receive the former No. 4 overall pick were not immediately available. The trade became official Monday, with the Texans sending draft picks to Arizona in exchange for Harrison and a draft pick in return.

The trade came at a crossroads for Arizona, which had lost three straight games before the deal was announced. Harrison's production had also been a point of discussion. In his time with the Cardinals this year, he recorded five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown in four games.

Now, the wide receiver is in a new organization and reunited with former Ohio State teammate and quarterback C.J. Stroud.

Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) celebrates a touchdown by wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18) during the first half of the NCAA football game against the Indiana Hoosiers at Ohio Stadium in Columbus, Ohio, on Nov. 12, 2022. Credit: Adam Cairns/Columbus Dispatch / USA TODAY NETWORK

"Just excited, man," Harrison said when asked about his initial reaction to finding out he was heading to Houston, according to NFL reporter Aaron Wilson. "Always watched Texas from afar. Obviously, just watching C.J. [Stroud], so pretty surreal to play with him now again. And as I said, just help him out the best I can."

The duo previously played two seasons together at Ohio State, where Harrison recorded 77 receptions for 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns in 2022, Stroud's final season as the starting quarterback. That reunion has Texans fans eager to see their chemistry translate to the NFL stage.

However, when Harrison was asked about his former club, the wide receiver was more reserved in his response.

Oct 19, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18) against the Green Bay Packers at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images

"I'll keep those things to myself," he said. "I'm really just moving forward."

While Harrison wasn't willing to share much about his departure from Arizona, his brief response left plenty unsaid. Now, with a fresh start in Houston alongside Stroud, the focus shifts to whether a reunion years in the making can help him turn the page on his time with the Cardinals.

articles.title: Seahawks Make Jaxon Smith-Njigba Announcement After Injury Update
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks named Jaxon Smith-Njigba a captain for Thursday's game against Denver, offering another positive development after his ankle injury. The...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have made another announcement involving star receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba ahead of Thursday's matchup against the Denver Broncos, this time with some encouraging news after his ankle injury.

Seattle announced Wednesday, October 14, that Smith-Njigba will serve as one of the team's three captains for Thursday Night Football, joining defensive tackle Byron Murphy II and fullback Brady Russell.

The Seahawks have rotated their game captains throughout the 2026 season, giving different players an opportunity to represent the team each week.

Smith-Njigba also reshared the team's announcement on his Instagram Story, acknowledging the honor ahead of a game in which Seattle is trying to rebound from consecutive losses.

It's a notable development for Smith-Njigba, who has been dealing with an ankle injury since Sunday's 32-29 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .

Jaxon Smith-Njigba Gets Positive Injury News Before Broncos Game

Smith-Njigba's availability had become a concern after the Seahawks listed him as a limited participant on their first two injury reports of the week.

He appeared to aggravate his ankle during the first half of Sunday's loss to San Francisco, receiving treatment and having the ankle taped before continuing to play.

Despite the injury, Smith-Njigba finished with five receptions for 102 yards and a touchdown.

Wednesday brought a positive development. Smith-Njigba participated fully in Seattle's final practice before traveling to Denver, and the Seahawks did not assign him an injury designation for Thursday.

Head coach Mike Macdonald confirmed the receiver's readiness during his October 14 press conference.

"Those guys, they're ready to play. Look good," Macdonald said when asked about Smith-Njigba and defensive tackle Leonard Williams, who has also been managing an ankle injury.

Smith-Njigba's captaincy announcement adds another encouraging note to a week that began with uncertainty surrounding his health.

Seahawks Star Faces Big Opportunity Against Injured Broncos Defense

Smith-Njigba has been Seattle's most productive offensive weapon through five games, recording 37 receptions for 583 yards and seven touchdowns.

He leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, having surpassed 100 receiving yards in four of Seattle's first five games.

Now, he enters Thursday's matchup with an intriguing opportunity against a Denver defense missing several important players.

The Broncos have ruled out All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga, both of whom are dealing with ankle injuries. Cornerback Riley Moss is also questionable with a rib injury.

That leaves Denver facing the NFL's leading receiver without its top cornerback, an unfavorable situation for a defense preparing for Seattle's passing attack.

Smith-Njigba will also have something to prove after Sunday's defeat.

Despite another 100-yard performance against San Francisco, the receiver took responsibility for a critical late drop that contributed to Seattle's inability to complete its comeback.

"I will learn from this and will be better. Our team will be better," Smith-Njigba said following the loss.

Three days later, the Seahawks have selected him to help lead the team into one of its most important early-season matchups.

Seattle enters Thursday at 3-2, looking to end a two-game losing streak and keep pace in the NFC West.

Smith-Njigba's ankle injury no longer carries a game designation. His role as one of Seattle's captains is official.

Now comes the opportunity to help deliver the response he promised after Sunday's defeat.
